Description: Fragments of a Hebrew Psalms copy from Qumran Cave 4, preserving parts of Psalm 89 (formerly catalogued as 4Q236). The verses survive in a non-Masoretic sequence within the fragment (verse 26 before verse 23). No date is stated for it in the published list consulted, so none is given here. Preserved-passage ranges for this manuscript are given in English (KJV) numbering; the manuscript itself carries no modern psalm numbers.
Significance: An early Hebrew witness to the Psalms, predating the medieval Masoretic manuscripts by about a thousand years. Its chief value is textual: it shows which psalms and which readings were already in circulation in the Second Temple period, and, where its psalm order differs from the Masoretic Psalter, that the order of the Psalter was not yet fully fixed.
